title: Forged & Sent · Architecture Atlas
product: Faith-centered workouts, discipleship and group accountability
overview: The Flutter client has its shell, Today and the day's devotional reading. A completed devotional is saved in the member's own SQLite file on the phone and nothing is sent anywhere. Firebase is connected only to local demo emulators. Workouts, sync, group roles, private reflections and production scoring are planned, not implemented.

systems.label: Behavioral prototype
systems.purpose: The archived HTML behavior is a reference for user experience only. It is not the production Flutter client or a trusted identity/data service.
systems.notes: Older snapshots stay available under versions/; no production persistence should be inferred.

systems.label: Flutter entrypoint
systems.purpose: main() initializes Flutter and switches between a local preview and emulator mode. Unsupported cloud modes are rejected without falling back to live Firebase.
systems.notes: Review mode selection and fail-closed behavior before any production backend is enabled.

systems.label: App shell and screens
systems.purpose: ForgedSentApp sets up MaterialApp and the six-tab shell. Today shows the date, mission line, progress ring and the day's boxes; the devotional box opens the day's reading. FoundationHomeScreen is the developer status page, reached from Settings and shown first when a start-up check fails.
systems.notes: Only the devotional box works. Five tabs are placeholders, and there is no workout feature yet.

systems.label: Today view model and rules
systems.purpose: A Riverpod view model combines the day's record, the streak, the bundled readings and one setting. A completion is an event with a client-generated id; an undo is a second event filed under the completion's day. One injected clock supplies the time, and days are a LocalDate.
systems.notes: No score is computed and nothing is sent. Point values are hidden unless the preview switch is on.

systems.label: Local store
systems.purpose: One SQLite file per owner, through Drift. A completion event and the day state it produces are written in one transaction. Before sign-in the owner is a local profile made on first launch. The web preview has no database and keeps the day in memory.
systems.notes: Events are stored locally only. There is no outbox and no sync yet, and no migration has been needed.

systems.label: Demo Firebase adapter
systems.purpose: ForgedFirebaseRuntime rejects non-demo Firebase projects, connects Auth/Firestore/Storage SDKs to local endpoints, and signs in anonymously to check reachability.
systems.notes: Anonymous sign-in is a local smoke test, not user authorization.

systems.label: Local Firebase
systems.purpose: Local Auth (9099), Firestore (8080) and Storage (9199) services used only with the demo-forgedandsent project.
systems.notes: Rules are deny-by-default outside owner-scoped developer_smoke paths. This is not production-ready group authorization.

systems.label: Developer bootstrap
systems.purpose: Guided setup scripts and Git helpers install development prerequisites and teach new contributors how to work on feature branches.
systems.notes: Hosted CI is not a substitute for a physical clean-machine acceptance test.

systems.label: Multi-agent review
systems.purpose: Reusable skills guide each provider; local review.py requests independent evidence-backed findings and records an advisory verdict without GitHub approval or merge powers.
systems.notes: CLI availability, authentication and actual two-provider review runs still need workstation verification.

systems.label: Required CI gate
systems.purpose: The active GitHub Actions ci-gate aggregates policy, Python tests, Flutter builds, Mac/Windows checks, iOS simulator and Firebase security-rule emulator tests. A separate functional-review status producer is staged but its ruleset is disabled.
systems.notes: A passing AI review never replaces GitHub checks or a human decision.

systems.label: ViewModels & commands
systems.purpose: Intended UI state holders translate commands into repository operations and immutable view state.
systems.notes: The first one exists: TodayViewModel, under Implemented. Others come with their features.

systems.label: Domain repositories
systems.purpose: Repository interfaces decouple UI and domain logic from Firebase and local storage. Use cases are added only when behavior warrants them.
systems.notes: DayRepository and SettingsRepository exist, under Implemented. Repositories for workouts, groups and the journal do not.

systems.label: Durable local outbox
systems.purpose: Persist workout events and unique idempotency keys before presenting a save as durable. Retry and reconcile on reconnect.
systems.notes: The local event store exists for devotional completions, under Implemented. The outbox that sends events does not. Firebase cache alone must not be treated as a durable event log.

systems.label: Sync coordinator
systems.purpose: Retries uploads, deduplicates event identifiers and reconciles offline edits with trusted server state.
systems.notes: Conflict policy, local store and data retention need ADRs.

systems.label: Service adapters
systems.purpose: Adapters translate repository operations to SDK/network calls while keeping SDK types out of Flutter widgets and domain interfaces.
systems.notes: The current emulator-only smoke adapter is not this full production data layer.

systems.label: Protected backend
systems.purpose: Trusted Firebase Security Rules, Auth claims and server-side checks enforce user and group permissions. Private prayers and measurements do not appear in group queries.
systems.notes: No real membership or private production model exists yet.

systems.label: Server scoring
systems.purpose: Trusted functions compute auditable group points and challenges from validated events. Clients cannot award authoritative points.
systems.notes: No server scoring functions exist yet.

systems.label: Branch & tests
systems.purpose: Create feature branch, implement a small vertical slice, update architecture when needed and run deterministic tests before AI calls.
systems.notes: A local hook is helpful but bypassable.

systems.label: Independent reviewers
systems.purpose: Non-author providers check bounded changes, record path/line findings and mark tool failures NOT VERIFIED. The authoring agent does not count as an independent reviewer. Local reviews are advisory; hosted review evidence is a separate staged process.
systems.notes: Review agents do not push, approve, merge or deploy.

systems.label: Draft PR & GitHub CI
systems.purpose: Push to a feature branch, open a Draft PR and require all aggregated ci-gate jobs to pass before merging.
systems.notes: Live human-approval count must be checked separately; AI advisory review cannot satisfy it.

systems.label: Hosted review evidence
systems.purpose: The staged GitHub workflow classifies functional changes and routes Codex-authored work to Claude subscription OAuth, Claude-authored work to native Codex GitHub Code Review, and verified same-repository Dependabot updates to Codex through trusted dispatch bound to the PR head. The scheduled reconciler with actions: write dispatches a gate run when native evidence appears or a bot PR head first needs review. The trusted publisher has pull-requests: write to post an implementor handoff and statuses: write for the exact-head gate status. A PR #48 branch-targeted run posted failure handoffs; a same-event main-ref run with issues: write alone still received HTTP 403. The local publisher API wrapper rejects PR review and state-mutation endpoints, but branch-targeted runs still check out default-branch code. Clean PASS handoff with the new code and final success remain unverified. The required-status ruleset is disabled.
systems.notes: AI findings are advisory, while GitHub rules can require a status after activation. No AI approval or merge authority is granted.

systems.label: Human merge decision
systems.purpose: A human inspects scope, risks, failures and GitHub status. Sensitive auth, data-access and scoring changes warrant another human reviewer even when not enforced.
systems.notes: No automatic merge permission is granted to agents.

symbolNotes.mobile/lib/main.dart::main: Initializes Flutter, opens the member's local store, reads FS_ENV, and starts the preview UI or connects the demo Firebase emulators. Rejects unsupported cloud modes.
symbolNotes.mobile/lib/src/app/forged_sent_app.dart:: Constructs the app under a provider scope: themes, the tab shell router, and a refresh of the day when the app is resumed.
The developer status page: local emulator status, or an explicit start-up or storage error.
symbolNotes.mobile/lib/src/firebase/forged_firebase_: Checks demo-only project ID, initializes Firebase with nonproduction options, redirects SDK calls to local ports 9099/8080/9199, then performs anonymous Auth smoke sign-in.
Chooses 127.0.0.1 for browser/desktop and 10.0.2.2 for the Android emulator unless a compile-time host override was provided.
symbolNotes.tooling/review/review.py::main: Parses CLI options, validates reviewer independence, prepares the diff, invokes reviewers and writes local advisory verdict reports.
symbolNotes.tooling/review/review.py::parse_report: Validates strict JSON review output, including severity, file/line evidence and contradictions between verdict and high-risk findings.
symbolNotes.tooling/review/review.py::verify: Checks that the locally saved passing review matches the current Git HEAD and diff, otherwise fails rather than trusting stale reviews.
symbolNotes.tooling/architecture/generate.py::invent: Produces the Markdown Flutter code map from actual Dart imports and named declarations.
symbolNotes.tooling/skills/sync.py::validate: Detects and can repair drift between canonical Codex and mirrored Claude skill files.
symbolNotes.mobile/lib/src/features/today/presentati: Builds Today's view from the day's record, the streak and the bundled content, and records Amen and Undo as completion events.
symbolNotes.mobile/lib/src/features/today/data/drift: Stores a completion event and the day state it produces in one transaction; a replayed event id changes nothing.
